2875b, take [1] Documented

IA transcribes 2875 B; DAHR gives 2875b and brackets the take number. The ten-inch master is one complete side; no concatenation.

Processing
Transferred at 78 rpm using four styli; engineer-preferred version selected Documented

The item specifies 3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil truncated-conical styli. Which stylus supplied this friendly filename, and any subsequent restoration, are not independently established.

The historical composition is separate from rights in this recording and transfer.

Recording rights
US public domain: recording first published before 1 January 1926 Documented

Rule 2. IA dates the recording 1902 and identifies matrix 2875 B; DAHR links that master to Gramophone 52440 and the V.A.30 reissue. The opened metadata has no licenseurl and no non-commercial licence. The later physical pressing date is not asserted as the original publication date.
